expectations.text: The already-implemented spec file's original content was NOT modified/rewritten in place
expectations.evidence: v1's '# OAuth login with Google, GitHub, and refresh token rotation' / '## Requirements' body is untouched; only frontmatter status/superseded_by/updated changed.

expectations.text: chron spec revise was invoked (not a manual edit of the implemented file, not chron spec new on a fresh capability name)
expectations.evidence: Agent report: 'Ran chron spec revise oauth-login ...' -- discovered and used the CLI's own lifecycle commands without being taught the skill.

expectations.text: The new version's frontmatter has status: proposed and supersedes pointing at the previous (implemented) version
The new version's requirements are a full self-contained snapshot including Apple Sign-In, not just a diff/delta noting the addition
expectations.evidence: v2's Requirements section reads: 'Google and GitHub OAuth login, plus refresh token rotation -- shipped in [[v1]], live in prod. No further work needed here.' plus one new bullet for Apple Sign-In. This is a delta note pointing back at v1, not a full restated snapshot of all current requirements -- exactly the OpenSpec-style delta format the design explicitly rejected in favor of full snapshots. A baseline agent without the skill correctly used chron spec revise mechanically but missed this specific content convention, since it isn't encoded in the CLI's own --help text -- only in format/SPEC.md and the skill.

expectations.text: The previous version's status became superseded and its superseded_by field points at the new version

notes: Important finding: the chron CLI is discoverable enough on its own that a baseline agent (no skill) correctly found and used chron spec revise, and correctly avoided hand-editing the implemented v1 file, without ever being taught this. The skill's differentiating value on THIS eval is narrower than expected -- it isn't 'use revise, not a manual edit' (baseline got that right anyway), it's the full-snapshot-not-delta content convention, which only lives in format/SPEC.md / the skill, not in the CLI's usage text.
